title: How to Use a Dough Scraper for Precise Sourdough Portioning
meta_description: Stop struggling with sticky dough! Learn how to portion sourdough dough using a bench scraper for perfectly sized loaves every single time.
html:
There is nothing more frustrating than finishing a long bulk fermentation only to realize your dough is a sticky, shapeless mass that refuses to cooperate. If you’ve ever tried to divide your dough with a knife or your hands, you know the struggle: the dough tears, sticks to everything, and you end up with one giant loaf and one tiny roll.

The secret to professional-looking loaves starts with the right tools. Learning how to portion sourdough dough effectively requires a bench scraper. This simple tool turns a messy process into a precise science, ensuring your loaves are consistent in weight and shape.

Why a Dough Scraper is Essential for Portioning

A dough scraper (also known as a bench scraper) is a flat, rectangular blade that allows you to cut through high-hydration dough without pulling or degassing it. When you use your hands, you tend to pull the dough, which can ruin the gluten structure you worked so hard to build during stretch-and-folds.

Using a tool like the one found in the 3-in-1 Sourdough Whisk Set (Whisk, Scraper, Lame) gives you a clean, vertical edge. This allows you to slice through the dough quickly and decisively. Because the blade is flat, it also helps you lift the dough off the counter without adding extra flour that could throw off your hydration levels.

Step-by-Step: How to Portion Sourdough Dough

To get perfectly sized loaves, you need to combine a digital scale with your scraper. Here is the most efficient way to handle the process:

  1. Prepare Your Station: Lightly dust your work surface with rice flour or bread flour. Avoid over-flouring, as too much can create a skin on your dough.
  2. The Initial Dump: Gently tip your bulked dough onto the counter. Use your scraper to nudge it into a rough rectangle.
  3. The Rough Cut: Decide how many loaves you are making. If you want two equal loaves, find the center point. Press the edge of your dough scraper straight down through the dough in one confident motion.
  4. The Precision Weigh: Use a bench scraper to lift one portion and place it on a digital scale. If it's too heavy, use the scraper to slice off a small sliver and move it to the other portion.
  5. The Quick Pre-Shape: Once weighed, use the scraper to tuck the edges of the dough toward the center, creating a round boule before you begin your final shaping.

Avoiding Common Mistakes When Portioning

One of the biggest mistakes beginners make is "sawing" the dough. If you move the scraper back and forth, you tear the gluten networks. Always use a single, decisive downward press. This keeps the interior of the loaf airy and open.

Another common issue is letting the dough stick to the tool. If you find the dough is clinging to your scraper, dip the blade in a tiny bit of water or a dusting of flour before you cut. If you are using the 3-in-1 Sourdough Whisk Set, you'll find the stainless steel surface is designed to release dough easily, but a quick wipe-down between cuts keeps things clean.

Integrating Your Tools for a Better Workflow

Baking sourdough is all about the sequence of tools. You start with the Danish dough whisk to incorporate your flour and water without overworking the dough. Once the bulk fermentation is complete, the dough scraper takes over for the portioning and pre-shaping we've discussed.

Finally, once your portioned loaves are shaped and proofed, the bread scoring lame completes the process. Having these three tools together—as seen in the 3-in-1 Sourdough Whisk Set (Whisk, Scraper, Lame)—ensures that you aren't hunting for a kitchen knife or a random spatula mid-bake, which can lead to the dough over-proofing while you search for your gear.

Tips for Handling High-Hydration Dough

If you are working with a very "wet" dough (80% hydration or higher), portioning becomes even more critical. High-hydration doughs tend to spread horizontally. To combat this, use your scraper to "square off" the dough before cutting. By creating a defined rectangular shape, you can more easily visualize where to divide the dough for equal portions.

Remember that the scraper isn't just for cutting; it's for managing. Use it to scrape the sides of your bowl during bulk fermentation to keep the dough moving and to clean your workspace so that flour doesn't build up into clumps that end up in your final bread.

FAQ

Can I use a regular knife to portion sourdough?

You can, but it's not recommended. Knives have a smaller surface area and often "drag" through the dough, which can tear the gluten. A dough scraper provides a wide, flat edge that cuts cleanly and allows you to lift the dough without sticking.

How do I clean my dough scraper?

Most stainless steel scrapers are dishwasher safe, but a quick rinse with warm soapy water immediately after use is best. This prevents dried dough from building up on the edges, which could cause sticking during your next bake.

What is the ideal weight for a standard sourdough loaf?

While it varies by preference, most home bakers aim for 800g to 1,000g per loaf. Using a scale and a scraper to divide your total batch weight by the number of loaves you want is the best way to ensure even baking times in the oven.
